PockPock Agent 0.2.14 fixes a PockPock Agent run that stopped with "The agent reached its tool-call limit" without writing anything. The agent could spend its whole budget reading the same files again and again. Plans also now reliably show the small actions under each step.

## Download

| Your computer | Download |
|---|---|
| Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) | [PockPock-Agent-Setup.exe](https://github.com/PockPock9/PockPockAgent/releases/latest/download/PockPock-Agent-Setup.exe) |
| Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or newer) | [PockPock-Agent-mac-arm64.dmg](https://github.com/PockPock9/PockPockAgent/releases/latest/download/PockPock-Agent-mac-arm64.dmg) |
| Mac with an Intel processor | [PockPock-Agent-mac-x64.dmg](https://github.com/PockPock9/PockPockAgent/releases/latest/download/PockPock-Agent-mac-x64.dmg) |

**Already using 0.2.13 on Windows?** PockPock updates itself: press **Restart to update** when it appears, or check in **Settings → Updates**. Your chats, settings, models and caches are kept. On a Mac, download and install it once, the same way as the first time.

**New to PockPock?** Open the downloaded file, then press **Set up PockPock**; setup installs everything else. Windows may show **"Windows protected your PC"** because PockPock is not code-signed yet: press **More info**, then **Run anyway**. On a Mac, see the [installation guide](https://github.com/PockPock9/PockPockAgent/wiki/Installation).

## What's new since 0.2.13

### Fewer wasted steps

A 6-step website task stopped at the tool-call limit after 19 calls that read files and wrote nothing. It now spends its calls on the work:

- **Bigger reads.** Reading a file returns up to 600 lines at a time instead of 160, so a typical file is read in one go.
- **Files read in parts can be replaced.** A long file read in parts, from the start, now counts as read in full. Before, a file longer than one read could never be replaced.
- **No re-reading after checks.** Running the project's checks no longer lets the agent read the same lines again; only a change to a file does.
- **No re-reading to prove the checks.** When the agent has to show evidence for the success checks, it is told to use what it has already read.
- **The limit grows with the plan.** A task may use 20 tool calls, plus 4 for every plan step beyond the third, up to 48. A 6-step plan gets 32.

### Small actions under every plan step

- The planner is now required to write the small actions for each step, one list per step. In 0.2.13 a small model could leave them out, and the plan showed none.
- Tested with `qwen3.5:9b` on a restaurant website request: each building step got three concrete actions, such as "create styles.css with a deep red and gold palette".

## Good to know

- The pull request passed the full check suite (backend tests and desktop typecheck and build on Ubuntu, Windows and macOS).
- Not tested yet: a full run of the website task with these changes.
